why: quotable numbers travel well on their own
posts:
I broke a normal 16-team school championship down into numbers.

Turns out the football is the smallest part of it.

Counting:

What happens on the pitch:

16 teams
176 players
31 matches
2 playing days

Four groups plus a knockout from the quarter-finals. Everything the spectators see.

What has to be recorded:

31 final scores
~90 goals with scorers
~50 assists
~40 cards

Each of these has to be written down at the moment it happens. Not after the match — at the moment.

What that becomes by hand:

5 minutes of collating after every match
2.5 hours of arithmetic across the tournament
4 group tables recalculated in full after every result
1 evening for the final report

And that is only the numbers.

It excludes entries, booking the hall, referees, messaging year groups, hunting for a spare ball and explaining team selection to parents.

2.5 hours is pure calculator time.

Which leads to a conclusion I resisted for a while:

A tournament is not an event. It is a dataset.

The football lasts two days. The data work lasts three weeks — before, during and after.

If you have run one, do the same maths on yours and post the number.

I am curious how many people turn 2.5 hours into five.
